itinerary.labelHtml:
The Itinerary

Day by day

Swipe each carousel for photos. Every stop carries its cost, a 💰 money-saving tip, an ✨ splurge, picky-kid restaurants, backup / if-time ideas, blog links, and a map — tap “Open in Google Maps” to navigate. Each day also shows an estimated per-day cost — food + activities only (excludes lodging, flights, and the rental car).

days.heading: Fly PIT to San Diego after work
days.note: This is the PTO trick: leave Thursday evening, sleep in California, and roll straight into the July 4th holiday weekend — Monday Jul 5 is the observed holiday, so the opening stretch costs only one PTO day (Fri Jul 2).

days.heading: July 4th-weekend beach day in La Jolla
days.note: Start with the most reliable water of the route. Keep it flexible: free beach/cove day if everyone is happy, kayak splurge if conditions are calm.

spots.cost: Beach and cove walks are free. Kayak/snorkel tours commonly run about $55-$90 per person; rent gear only if the water feels good.
spots.climate: Early July: San Diego ocean averages about 66-68 F. Swimmable for hardy kids, better with rash guards or short wetsuits; afternoons usually feel much warmer on sand.
spots.saveHtml: Save Make the main day free: La Jolla Shores swim, Cove sea lions from the sidewalk, picnic lunch, sunset tidepools.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Book a La Jolla sea-cave kayak tour for the 13-year-old adventure factor; budget roughly $250-$350 family depending operator and age rules.
spots.restoHtml:
• Wheat & Water — La Jolla casual spot with burgers, sandwiches, pasta, and pizza-style comfort food
  • Burger Lounge La Jolla — burgers, fries, chicken bites, shakes; reliable picky-kid backup
  • The Spot La Jolla — burgers, fries, pizza, pasta, and wings in the village
spots.altboxHtml:
• Mission Bay ↩ — flatter water, easier parking, and paddleboard rentals if the ocean is rough.
  • USS Midway Museum ↗ — ships, aircraft, and harbor time if the family wants an indoor/outdoor museum instead of zoo time.
  • Torrey Pines State Natural Reserve ↗ — short cliff walks and ocean views when you want nature over a beach sit.

days.heading: San Diego Zoo and Balboa Park
days.note: Use the bus tour early and do not fight the whole park in peak heat. This is the major San Diego paid anchor.

spots.name: San Diego Zoo + Balboa Park
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · San Diego ZooIG · Balboa ParkFlickr
spots.cost: Official 1-Day Any Day: adult ages 12+ $78, child ages 3-11 $68. With a 13-year-old and 8-year-old, family estimate is $302. No reservation required for standard tickets.
spots.climate: Early July: usually mild to warm, but the zoo is hilly. Start early, use the bus tour, and save indoor museums or hotel pool for late afternoon.
spots.saveHtml: Save Bring refillable bottles and snacks; the ticket already includes Guided Bus Tour and Skyfari subject to availability.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge If this is the flagship kid day, add one upgraded wildlife experience only after checking age rules and heat.
spots.restoHtml:
• Wheat & Water — La Jolla casual spot with burgers, sandwiches, pasta, and pizza-style comfort food
  • Burger Lounge La Jolla — burgers, fries, chicken bites, shakes; reliable picky-kid backup
  • The Spot La Jolla — burgers, fries, pizza, pasta, and wings in the village
spots.altboxHtml:
• USS Midway Museum ↩ — better if the family wants ships, aircraft, and harbor time instead of an all-day zoo.
  • Torrey Pines State Natural Reserve ↗ — short cliff walks and ocean views when you want nature over a beach sit.
  • Birch Aquarium ↗ — compact marine-life backup near La Jolla for heat, clouds, or short attention spans.

days.heading: Coronado, Mission Bay, or Torrey Pines
days.note: Keep the final San Diego day low-stress before the first long transfer. Coronado is easy; Torrey Pines is the nature swap.

spots.name: Coronado Beach + Mission Bay
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · CoronadoIG · Mission BayFlickr
spots.cost: Beach day is free except parking, bikes, snacks, or chair rentals. Budget $80-$180 for bikes or bay rentals if you make it active.
spots.climate: Early July: ocean is still cool but this is the best latitude for swimming on the route. Use hotel pool or Mission Bay if surf is rough.
spots.saveHtml: Save Pack towels and use Coronado as a low-cost recovery day after the zoo.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Rent bikes or a surrey near Coronado, or do a Mission Bay paddleboard session.
spots.restoHtml:
• Wheat & Water — La Jolla casual spot with burgers, sandwiches, pasta, and pizza-style comfort food
  • Burger Lounge La Jolla — burgers, fries, chicken bites, shakes; reliable picky-kid backup
  • The Spot La Jolla — burgers, fries, pizza, pasta, and wings in the village
spots.altboxHtml:
• Torrey Pines State Natural Reserve ↩ — swap in for cliffs and a short hike if the family wants nature over beach.
  • Birch Aquarium ↗ — compact marine-life backup near La Jolla for heat, clouds, or short attention spans.
  • Balboa Park gardens ↗ — free/low-cost wandering if the zoo price or stamina does not fit the day.

days.heading: Drive north through OC/LA to Santa Barbara
days.note: This is why OC/LA is not a base: it is worth a stop, but not worth adding a hotel move and traffic-heavy backtracking.

spots.cost: Beach/town stop is free; expect paid parking and lunch. Use it as a 2-3 hour break, not a base.
spots.climate: Early July: water usually similar to San Diego but slightly variable; swimmable for a short stop, with marine layer possible.
spots.saveHtml: Save Stop once in Laguna or Santa Monica, not both. Every extra LA-area stop costs traffic time.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Choose a beach-view lunch if traffic is good; otherwise keep moving and spend the money in Santa Barbara.
spots.restoHtml:
• Lucky Penny — Funk Zone wood-fired pizza; easy Margherita/plain cheese order
  • Brophy Bros. — harbor restaurant with kid-friendly pasta, fish and chips, cheeseburger, and fries
  • Finney's Crafthouse Santa Barbara — kids burgers, grilled cheese, crispy chicken bites, fries, and broad adult menu
spots.altboxHtml:
• Santa Monica Pier ↩ — more classic LA iconography, but usually more traffic and parking hassle.
  • Santa Barbara Mission ↗ — short history-and-garden add-on when the waterfront is foggy or windy.
  • Ventura Harbor Village ↗ — easy food, boats, and ice cream if the drive needs a low-effort stop.

days.heading: Santa Barbara waterfront and town
days.note: This is the classic Santa Barbara day: beach in the morning, town when the marine layer burns off, pizza or harbor dinner.

spots.name: Santa Barbara Waterfront + Courthouse
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · Santa BarbaraFlickr
spots.cost: Beach, Stearns Wharf, Funk Zone wandering, and the courthouse exterior are free. Bike rentals or surreys can push the day to $80-$180.
spots.climate: Early July: Santa Barbara summer ocean averages around 62-66 F. Great for beach play and brave dips; not warm like the Atlantic or Gulf.
spots.saveHtml: Save Use the free waterfront, courthouse tower/gardens when open, and picnic from a market.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Rent bikes along Cabrillo Boulevard or book a harbor kayak if the wind is calm.
spots.restoHtml:
• Lucky Penny — Funk Zone wood-fired pizza; easy Margherita/plain cheese order
  • Brophy Bros. — harbor restaurant with kid-friendly pasta, fish and chips, cheeseburger, and fries
  • Finney's Crafthouse Santa Barbara — kids burgers, grilled cheese, crispy chicken bites, fries, and broad adult menu
spots.altboxHtml:
• Butterfly Beach ↩ — prettier sand-and-sunset option if East Beach feels ordinary.
  • Ventura Harbor Village ↗ — easy food, boats, and ice cream if the drive needs a low-effort stop.
  • Crystal Cove State Park ↗ — better coast-and-tidepool stop than a generic freeway break if timing allows.

days.heading: Hearst Castle, elephant seals, and Big Sur to Monterey
days.note: Leave early. Highway 1 is the point today, but it is narrow, slow, and easy to overstuff with pullouts.

spots.name: Hearst Castle + Big Sur Coast
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · Hearst CastleIG · Big SurFlickr
spots.cost: Hearst Castle Grand Rooms/major daytime tours are $35 adult, $18 child ages 5-12, including $5.50 registration fee. Family estimate with a 13-year-old: $123. Reserve up to 60 days ahead.
spots.climate: Early July: Central Coast marine layer is common. Big Sur water is too cold for family swimming; plan viewpoints, short walks, and layers.
spots.saveHtml: Save If the day is running long, skip the castle interior and use the free elephant seal viewpoint plus Big Sur pullouts.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Keep the timed Grand Rooms Tour and build a slow lunch/photo day around it.
spots.restoHtml:
• Sardine Factory — children's menu lists cheese pizza, plain/butter pasta, mini burgers, and chicken strips
  • Rosine's Restaurant — casual Monterey comfort food, pasta, burgers, sandwiches, breakfast, and big desserts
  • Melville Tavern — burgers, pasta, ribs, salads, and straightforward tavern food
spots.altboxHtml:
• Morro Bay ↩ — a gentler lunch and harbor stop if Big Sur weather or traffic looks bad.
  • Elephant Seal Vista Point ↗ — free wildlife stop just north of San Simeon if the kids need a break.
  • Moonstone Beach Boardwalk ↗ — flat ocean walk with driftwood and tide views, easier than a long cliff stop.

days.heading: Monterey Bay Aquarium and Cannery Row
days.note: The aquarium is worth paying for once. Pair it with the free coastal trail so the day does not become wall-to-wall paid attractions.

spots.name: Monterey Bay Aquarium + Cannery Row
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · Monterey Bay AquariumIG · Cannery RowFlickr
spots.cost: Official tickets through Sep 7, 2026: adult $65, youth ages 5-17 $50. Family estimate: $230. Advance purchase recommended for smooth entry.
spots.climate: Early July: Monterey water is usually around 55-58 F. Great for otters, kelp forest, tidepools, and jackets; not normal swimming water.
spots.saveHtml: Save Do the aquarium as the paid anchor and keep Cannery Row/Coastal Trail as the free half of the day.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Add one behind-the-scenes or feeding experience only if the kids are aquarium people.
spots.restoHtml:
• Sardine Factory — children's menu lists cheese pizza, plain/butter pasta, mini burgers, and chicken strips
  • Rosine's Restaurant — casual Monterey comfort food, pasta, burgers, sandwiches, breakfast, and big desserts
  • Melville Tavern — burgers, pasta, ribs, salads, and straightforward tavern food
spots.altboxHtml:
• Pacific Grove tidepools ↩ — free, wild, and easy if the aquarium crowd is too much.
  • Carmel Beach ↗ — less logistics and more sand if the family is done with trails.
  • Lovers Point Park ↗ — protected cove, lawn, and snack access for a shorter coast stop.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Official aquarium tickets ↗Monterey Coastal Trail ↗

days.heading: Point Lobos, Carmel, and 17-Mile Drive
days.note: This is the best nature/town blend on the Central Coast. Get to Point Lobos early or very late for parking sanity.

spots.name: Point Lobos + Carmel + 17-Mile Drive
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · Point LobosIG · CarmelIG · 17-Mile DriveFlickr
spots.cost: Point Lobos vehicle day use is $10. 17-Mile Drive day-guest admission is currently $12.50 per vehicle and reimbursable with qualifying Pebble Beach resort restaurant purchase.
spots.climate: Early July: cool coast and high-50s ocean. Bring layers even if Carmel village is sunny.
spots.saveHtml: Save Arrive at Point Lobos before 9:30 or after 3:00; parking is limited and walking in can save the vehicle fee if safe/legal parking is available.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Do 17-Mile Drive slowly and use the reimbursable gate fee toward a Pebble Beach snack stop.
spots.restoHtml:
• Sardine Factory — children's menu lists cheese pizza, plain/butter pasta, mini burgers, and chicken strips
  • Rosine's Restaurant — casual Monterey comfort food, pasta, burgers, sandwiches, breakfast, and big desserts
  • Melville Tavern — burgers, pasta, ribs, salads, and straightforward tavern food
spots.altboxHtml:
• Carmel Beach sunset ↩ — less logistics and more sand if the family is done with trails.
  • Lovers Point Park ↗ — protected cove, lawn, and snack access for a shorter coast stop.
  • Dennis the Menace Playground ↗ — simple kid reset near downtown when adults need a low-pressure afternoon.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Official Point Lobos info ↗17-Mile Drive fee FAQ ↗

days.heading: Santa Cruz and coastal drive into San Francisco

facts.label: Stop
facts.valueHtml: Santa Cruz or Half Moon Bay

days.note: Keep moving north. Drop the car after arrival if the hotel parking math is ugly.

spots.name: Santa Cruz Boardwalk + Coastal Drive
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · Santa Cruz BoardwalkFlickr
spots.cost: Boardwalk entry is free; rides/arcade/food are pay-as-you-go. Budget $150-$250 if everyone rides and snacks.
spots.climate: Early July: beach weather can be sunny or foggy; water remains cold enough that this is rides, sand, and surf-watching more than swimming.
spots.saveHtml: Save Use the Boardwalk as a leg stretch and buy only a few rides instead of all-day wristbands.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Stay longer for classic rides, mini golf, and arcade if the kids need a pure fun day before San Francisco.
spots.restoHtml:
• Golden Boy Pizza — North Beach square slices; cheese pizza is the easy win
  • The Codmother Fish & Chips — fish and chips, fries, shrimp, tacos; simple fried-food backup by the Wharf
  • Super Duper Burgers — burgers, chicken sandwich, fries, shakes, and several SF locations
spots.altboxHtml:
• Half Moon Bay ↩ — quieter coastal bluffs and seafood-town feel if rides are not the mood.
  • Dennis the Menace Playground ↗ — simple kid reset near downtown when adults need a low-pressure afternoon.
  • Point Pinos Lighthouse ↗ — small historic stop with coastal wandering nearby.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Santa Cruz Boardwalk ↗Half Moon Bay guide ↗
spots.spotMapHtml: 📍 Open in Google Maps ↩

days.heading: Golden Gate, Presidio, and Crissy Field
days.note: A free-heavy San Francisco day balances the expensive Aquarium/Alcatraz tickets. Add Exploratorium if fog or kid energy points indoors.

spots.name: Golden Gate Bridge + Presidio
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · Golden Gate BridgeIG · PresidioFlickr
spots.cost: Bridge viewpoints, Crissy Field, Tunnel Tops, and much of the Presidio are free. Budget for rideshare/bikes/snacks.
spots.climate: Early July: San Francisco can be windy and foggy; ocean averages around 56-58 F. Bring hoodies even if the day starts warm.
spots.saveHtml: Save Drop the rental car first, then use rideshare/transit. Avoiding hotel parking can save $180-$270 over three nights.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Rent bikes for the bridge/Marina route if fog and wind are friendly.
spots.restoHtml:
• Golden Boy Pizza — North Beach square slices; cheese pizza is the easy win
  • The Codmother Fish & Chips — fish and chips, fries, shrimp, tacos; simple fried-food backup by the Wharf
  • Super Duper Burgers — burgers, chicken sandwich, fries, shakes, and several SF locations
spots.altboxHtml:
• Exploratorium ↩ — excellent bad-weather backup and especially strong for an 8-year-old.
  • Lands End ↗ — dramatic coastal walk when the family wants views instead of another pier.
  • Crissy Field ↗ — flat Golden Gate views, beach, and picnic space without bridge parking stress.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Presidio bridge guide ↗SF ocean temps ↗
spots.spotMapHtml: 📍 Open in Google Maps ↩

days.heading: Alcatraz and Fisherman's Wharf
days.note: Book official Alcatraz tickets as soon as the date enters the 90-day window. In summer, waiting turns this into a resale or replacement problem.

spots.name: Alcatraz + Fisherman's Wharf
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · AlcatrazIG · Fisherman's WharfFlickr
spots.cost: NPS-listed Day Tour: adult/youth 12+ $47.95, child 5-11 $29.15. Family estimate with a 13-year-old and 8-year-old: $173. Buy official ferry tickets up to 90 days ahead.
spots.climate: Early July: cold wind on the bay is normal. Dress warmer than the city forecast suggests.
spots.saveHtml: Save Book the official Day Tour, not a bundled reseller, unless official tickets are already sold out.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Night Tour is pricier but memorable; with younger kids, only choose it if late/cold evenings are okay.
spots.restoHtml:
• Golden Boy Pizza — North Beach square slices; cheese pizza is the easy win
  • The Codmother Fish & Chips — fish and chips, fries, shrimp, tacos; simple fried-food backup by the Wharf
  • Super Duper Burgers — burgers, chicken sandwich, fries, shakes, and several SF locations
spots.altboxHtml:
• Bay cruise without island landing ↩ — easier if Alcatraz is sold out or the family wants views without the prison tour.
  • Exploratorium ↗ — excellent bad-weather backup and especially strong for an 8-year-old.
  • Crissy Field ↗ — flat Golden Gate views, beach, and picnic space without bridge parking stress.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Official NPS Alcatraz fees ↗Official tour operator note ↗

days.heading: Fly SFO to PIT
days.note: If flying east with a connection, keep the morning simple and stay near transit/rideshare access the night before.

Plan Health-Check

What to lock, watch, and expect

Research updated July 2026 for a family of 4, with kids age 13 and 8 in trip year 2027. The earlier Jun 17-29 Juneteenth window sits inside the Jun 23-26 Pittsburgh blackout, so this version moves to Jul 1-13, 2027, anchored on the observed Independence Day holiday (Mon Jul 5).

PTO win

Independence Day lines up correctly in 2027

The 2027 calendar works: Thursday Jul 1 evening departure, Independence Day observed Monday Jul 5, and Tuesday Jul 13 return gives 12 nights for about 7 PTO days. The window also clears the Jun 23-26 Pittsburgh blackout with days to spare; the tradeoff is July 4th-weekend crowds and lodging pressure in San Diego, so book that base early.

Book first

Alcatraz and coastal lodging are the squeeze points

Alcatraz official tickets are sold up to 90 days ahead and peak summer dates sell out weeks ahead. Coastal family rooms in La Jolla, Santa Barbara, Carmel/Monterey, and Fisherman's Wharf price high and should be locked early.

Cold water

Only Southern California is casual-swim territory

Early-July San Diego water is typically 66-68 F; Santa Barbara is more like 62-66 F; Monterey and San Francisco hover around the high 50s. Treat north-coast water as toe-dip, kayak, tidepool, or wetsuit water.

Road reality

Big Sur is open, beautiful, and slow

Highway 1 through Big Sur reopened in 2026 after Regent's Slide, but it remains a narrow two-lane cliff road with landslide risk, construction delays, limited cell service, and many pullouts. Do not plan it like a freeway leg.

Rental car

One-way drop fees are quote-specific

California one-way rentals often show the drop cost inside the rate rather than as a clean line item. Current aggregators show low daily base rates, but a family-size SUV/minivan plus airport fees and one-way pricing can still land around $850-$1,450 even after trimming three days.

Now fixed

Length verdict: 12 nights is just right

The prior 13-night version was one night too much for the $12k/$15k budget. Twelve nights keeps the San Diego-to-San Francisco arc intact, avoids rushing the Central Coast, and pulls the high end below the hard cap.

Picky eaters

Every base has plain-food fallbacks

Each base includes real restaurants with pizza, pasta, burgers, fries, chicken, or kid-menu basics so seafood-heavy coast days do not become dinner negotiations.

Best Time to Go

July 4 is the PTO win

The Juneteenth window (Jun 17-29) conflicts with the Jun 23-26 Pittsburgh blackout, so the trip moves to Jul 1-13. In 2027, July 4 falls on Sunday and is observed on Monday, July 5.

Recommended

Thu Jul 1-Tue Jul 13

Depart after work Thursday, sleep in San Diego that night, ride the July 4th holiday weekend (observed Mon Jul 5) for two free vacation days, and return Tuesday after 12 nights.

PTO count

About 7 work days

With Independence Day observed Monday Jul 5, PTO is Fri Jul 2, Jul 6-9, and Jul 12-13 — seven days. That is the best post-blackout budget/PTO geometry for a domestic route that still feels complete.

Why shorter

13 nights was too costly

The old length added an expensive Santa Barbara night after the route already had enough coastal-town time.

Verdict: 12 nights is just right for California under the $15k cap. Thirteen is nicer but cap-risky; 10-11 nights starts making the Central Coast feel rushed.

Save money

  • Drop the car before San Francisco. Three nights of city parking can cost $180-$270 before stress.
  • Keep OC/LA as a stop, not a base. This avoids one hotel move and one traffic-heavy local day.
  • Use free coast days. La Jolla, Coronado, Santa Barbara waterfront, Carmel Beach, Crissy Field, and the Presidio can carry full days.
  • Buy only the major tickets that matter. Zoo, Hearst, Aquarium, and Alcatraz are enough; do not stack every museum.
  • Stay in Monterey over Carmel if budget tightens. You keep the same nature access and usually save meaningfully.
  • Quote rental pickup/drop combinations. SAN airport to SFO airport, SAN to downtown SF, and off-airport returns can price differently.

  • La Jolla kayak or snorkel tour. Best paid water memory if conditions are calm.
  • Pool-forward San Diego lodging. It protects the water target when the Pacific feels cold.
  • Hearst Castle timed tour. It turns the long Santa Barbara-to-Monterey transfer into a real destination day.
  • Monterey Bay Aquarium. Expensive, but one of the strongest family stops on the route.
  • Alcatraz official tour. Worth it if booked early at normal price.

Travel Tips

The stuff nobody tells you

Operational notes updated July 2026; re-check live road, ticket, and fare data before paying.

Book in roughly this order

  1. Flights · as soon as dates are locked
  2. Coastal lodging · immediately after flights
  3. Rental car · quote early, re-check weekly
  4. Alcatraz · 90 days ahead
  5. Hearst Castle · up to 60 days ahead
  6. Monterey Bay Aquarium · advance purchase
  7. San Diego Zoo · buy online; no standard reservation required

  • Tickets

    Where timing matters

    • Alcatraz. Official ferry tickets are the only island access and can be purchased up to 90 days ahead.
    • Hearst Castle. Tours leave at the printed time; arrive at least 20 minutes early.
    • Aquarium. Advance purchase is recommended even when timed entry is not the same kind of bottleneck as Alcatraz.

  • Water

    Set expectations by latitude

    • San Diego. Cool but usable for hardy swimmers in early July, especially with sun and rash guards.
    • Santa Barbara. Pretty beach weather, colder water; plan shorter dips and more sand/bike time.
    • Monterey/SF. Do not sell these as swim bases; plan jackets, tidepools, boats, and viewpoints.

  • Driving

    Make transfers part of the trip

    • LA traffic. Leave San Diego after breakfast or before the worst afternoon pattern; pick one OC/LA stop.
    • Big Sur. Open as of current checks, but slow and slide-prone; check Caltrans/Big Sur Chamber the week of travel.
    • Northbound compromise. Southbound has easier ocean pullouts, but northbound is correct for the open-jaw route and no-backtrack rule.

  • Food

    Picky-eater safety net

    • Every base. Has pizza, pasta, burger, fries, or chicken backups in the plan.
    • Bookable dinners. Use reservations in Santa Barbara, Carmel, and San Francisco if dining after 6:30.
    • Snack bag. Keep it stocked for Big Sur, where services are sparse and expensive.

  • Lodging

    Where to spend

    • San Diego. Pool/parking/location matter more than luxury decor.
    • Santa Barbara. West Beach/Lower State reduces car use during the middle base.
    • San Francisco. Do not keep a rental car unless the hotel includes parking.

blocks.note: These are the tasks with real external release windows or limited capacity.
items: Alcatraz opens up to 90 days ahead; book if it matters to the San Francisco stop (NPS).
Muir Woods requires parking/shuttle reservations, with advance/day-of inventory subject to availability (Go Muir Woods).
Hearst Castle tours open up to 60 days ahead; reserve if the route includes San Simeon (Hearst Castle).

blocks.title: Final checks
items: REAL ID check: every traveler 18+ should have a REAL ID-compliant license or passport for domestic flights; TSA enforcement began in 2025 (TSA).
Insurance: compare family medical/trip coverage after the first meaningful deposit; waiver timing is policy-specific, so do not wait until final payment if coverage matters.
Offline kit: download confirmations, maps, rental contracts, gate codes, and backup contact numbers.
Check coastal fog, marine-layer forecasts, and road closures before locking each drive day.

preDepartureTodos.callout: Why this no longer says "act now" for flights: U.S. summer cash fares usually improve much closer in. Google Flights shows July/August domestic lows around 13-43 days out, Going uses 1-3 months as the domestic window, and Expedia 2026 Air Hacks found 180+ day domestic bookings were the most expensive category in its 2026 data. For family trips, start alerts earlier and buy on the early side of the window when schedule quality matters.
